issue_title: [CO] Unable to change existing CMS Page's category association (EASY FIX)
issue_body:

#### Describe the bug

Impossible to change CMS Category on a CMS Page

#### Why

Regression introduced in 1.7, in eb4cba2, see https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/commit/eb4cba22bd5769a16c147626c5ea9dc53a545f4e#r44998939
assertCmsCategoryExists has **no return statement**
still used in if clause asking for **true**

The AbstractCmsPageHandler.assertCmsCategoryExists() never returns a value.
See AddCmsPageHandler implementation (not using if clause).

Either move assertion inside if statement or add return statement to AbstractCmsPageHandler.assertCmsCategoryExists().

https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/1c565a28540b55e11b07c69905dbb1014ea162dd/src/Adapter/CMS/Page/CommandHandler/EditCmsPageHandler.php#L82

#### Expected behavior

Should be possible to change CMS Category on a CMS Page

#### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Try to reassign category on an existing CMS Page
2. Save, see that it was not persisted


#### Additional information

* PrestaShop version: 1.7.7.0
* PHP version: 7.3

title: Fixed case where saving virtual product attachment is modifying product price if a specific price is set on the product
issue_title: Saving virtual product attachment is modifying product price if a specific price is set on the product
issue_body:
#### Describe the bug

When using virtual products, retail price is getting modified during attachment save 
if there is a specific price set on the product.

#### Expected behavior

We expect the price remain the same , this is quite major issue as it messed up a lot of product prices in one of 
our customer shop.

#### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a "virtual product" with Retail Price Tax Inc  € 10.00
2. Add a specific price on the product (10% discount for ALL customers)
3. Go in "Virtual product" and add a file attachment, then click SAVE to confirm the attachment
4. Refresh the page and check the retail price again - It had been set to €9.00 (!)  - SAVING the attachment again will cause the price to get lowered again and again..

#### Additional information

Issue was debugged thanks to the help of M4 module creator.

The wrong line of the code is:

**$productAdapter->getProduct()** in **saveAction** method on **VirtualProductController** 
This method sets the product price using any specific price and later saves this wrong price.

* PrestaShop version: 1.7.6.9
* PHP version: 7.2

title: Fix legacy form selectors
issue_title: In BO some JavaScript parts relied on form field's ids and attributes that are modified since 1.7.8
issue_body:
<!--
****************************
DO NOT disclose security issues here, contact security@prestashop.com instead!
****************************
-->

#### Describe the bug
Since we split configuration forms into independent forms (#17819), id and name attributes in forms have changed, for example name attribute `form[general][enable_tos]` became `general[enable_tos]`, and its ID went from `form_general_enable_tos_0` to `general_enable_tos_0`. 

It is breaking some behaviors because sometimes we  have javascript relying on these attributes, also it is a breaking change for some modules that might rely on it too. This is among other things the cause of this issue: #21037

#### Expected behavior

There are two possibilities:

1/ We own the breaking change, write a doc about it, and we fix our javascript where it relies on former attributes.

2/ We find a way to make it so that the attributes remain as they were before, modifying Symfony's default naming. But we'd still have to fix other javascript pieces that relied on the new attributes.


#### Additional information

* PrestaShop version: develop
* PHP version: not relevant

title: Fix symfony cache clear
issue_title: Cache clear issue after optimization
issue_body:
<!--
****************************
DO NOT disclose security issues here, contact security@prestashop.com instead!
****************************
-->

#### Describe the bug

The way PrestaShop clears Symfony cache has been modified by this PR https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/20942

Although it is more performant, it also doesn't clear everything we need because the container is not rebuilt.
Among the things that I fear might be involved:
- Symfony routing updated
- Doctrine entities management
- Module's services updated

At least the routing has been proved to be failing with the module `ps_linklist` the other two remain to be confirmed, `productcomments` which uses both seemed to be fine but it's hard to tell if it's because the container was fully rebuilt after its installation.

The `Cache clear` feature is also impacted since it relies on the same method `SymfonyCacheClearer::clear`

#### Expected behavior

The Symfony cache should be completely cleared to ensure the container is correctly rebuilt with up to date information. However we must keep in mind that these two issues are still correctly handled:
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/20852
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/11105

#### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior (bug for routing at least):

1. Go to Module Manager
2. Uninstall `ps_linklist`
3. Remove the cache manually: `rm -fR ./var/cache/*`
4. Go to Module Catalog
5. Refresh the page so that the menu is updated (this should be handled by MBO)
6. Click on Design > LinkWidget
7. See the error from screenshot, the url should be managed by Symfony router via the `_legacy_link` property but since the Router info were not updated it tries to access the legacy controller which does not exist any more

**Screenshots**

![Capture d’écran 2020-10-13 à 12 31 01](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13801017/95851809-13c42380-0d53-11eb-9576-55bd161ef3f1.png)

#### Potential solution

We need to revert the command used back to `cache:clear` however it cause some issues because the memory limit was reached So one possibility is to dynamically force the memory_limit when we perform this command

#### Additional information

* PrestaShop version: 1.7.8
* PHP version: N/A

#### Describe the bug

There is an error in selecting the correct language when using a multishop and different languages for each store. 

 For example, let's assume that we have two shops (multistore) in the same domain with a virtual URL for each one:

SHOPA is using www.teststore.com/shopa with only English as a main and default language.
SHOPB is using www.teststore.com/shopb with only Spanish as a main and default language. 

English is only associated to ShopA and Spanish is only associated to ShopB. 

Both stores are in the same group. 

If you go to SHOPB you can see all the information in spanish, but if you access SHOPA then the selected language from the cookie is Spanish wich is not associated to SHOPA. 

This error is created in the config.inc.php file 

#### Expected behavior

When changing shops the id_lang from the cookie should be checked and validated in the config.inc.php before start loading the translations. 

#### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create two shops in the same group, assign the same domain and a virtual url for each one.
2. Assign one language to SHOP A and other Language to SHOPB , different languages for both and only associated one language per store. 
3. Go to SHOPA and then go to SHOPB, the language in SHOPB is the language set in SHOPA (To validate this just dump($context->language) in config.inc.php around line 200).
